subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a default subagent tool-inactivity watchdog with nudge then abort semantics, or should recovery depend first on the broader session activity, watchdog, and manual-control design?
rationale: The remaining work adds config/default behavior, automatic kill policy, model-visible injected messages, per-spawn override policy, and channel-visible recovery semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Core Subagent Recovery
options.body: Keep this issue as the subagent-specific product slice and define guarded defaults, nudge copy, abort semantics, parent notification, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Depend On Activity API First
options.body: Keep the issue open but make #39127 and #39141 prerequisites so recovery consumes a single activity and attention source.

options.title: Limit Core To Timeout And Manual Control
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge and kill defaults now; rely on runTimeoutSeconds and a separate manual kill or reap surface if maintainers decide automatic abort is too risky.

recommendation.title: Design Core Subagent Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the subagent-specific product slice and define guarded defaults, nudge copy, abort semantics, parent notification, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across subagent timeout enforcement, lifecycle handling, kill reconciliation, and recovery-sensitive runtime policy.
